en: The General Meaning of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, composed by Hengming Guting Shanjian.
The doctrine of the Avataṃsaka is vast and its text is extensive; it is difficult for anyone who has not fully grasped its subtleties to [comprehend it].
Pen and tongue. The Elder Vairocana’s single true samādhi is, within the sphere of the person, most authentic and most vital.
Whether one opens the mouth to speak or does not open the mouth to speak, it is spoken in both cases; whether opening the mouth or not opening the mouth, it is spoken in all instances.
All Buddha-dharma, all profound mysteries, all functional applications, all seizing and raising [the whisk], all blows and shouts—all of these.
Regarding language, all written characters, and all samādhis: when employed, they are employed collectively; when not employed, they are not employed collectively.
Whether employed or not employed, they do not obstruct one another at all. When the World-Honored One ascended the seat, Mañjuśrī struck the gavel and said:

"Contemplate clearly the Dharma of the Dharma-King; the Dharma of the Dharma-King is thus. Thereupon, the World-Honored One descended from the seat. This was precisely the point where Mañjuśrī opened his mouth to act.
The World-Honored One descended from his seat; this is the point where he did not open his mouth. Arriving here, what did the World-Honored One say?
If you say he said something, Mañjuśrī was already mistaken. If you say he said nothing, the World-Honored One’s ascent of the seat was likewise a mistake.
Speaking of the great meaning of the Flower Treasury (Avataṃsaka), whether there was speaking or no speaking, whether there was error or no error—it lies beyond opening or not opening the mouth.
In the space of a single glance, not a single point can be hidden from others. For instance, when Zhaozhou asked Touzi, "What is it like when one who has died the great death returns to life?
Touzi replied, "Night travel is not permitted; you must arrive early at dawn. Such a question and answer are like the conversation of ordinary people;
yet they neither created a deliberate opportunity nor were they contrived as Chan, the Way, or the Buddha.
Dharma assembly! You are in the south of the Yangtze; I am in the north of the Hupei. You are in the heavens; I am in the human realm.

Throughout the four quarters and eight directions, there is nowhere where we do not correspond. If one does not reach such a state, then even if one were to spit out the entirety of the Great Canon of the Buddha’s teachings in a single breath—piling them like mountains and filling the seas—it would all be of no use.
Before the World-Honored One had ascended the seat, and before Mañjuśrī had made his formal address.
The Mallet: Before Zhaozhou and Touzi had even met, they had already handed over their entire capacity.
Even all the Buddhas and spiritual friends throughout the fragrant water-seas of the Avataṃsaka Dharma-realm would have no place to set hand or foot. As the Sūtra says:
"The profound realm of the Tathāgata is equal in measure to empty space; all sentient beings enter it, yet in reality there is nothing entered. Since...
There is nothing to enter; how could there be anything to explain? Beyond this, no further expedient means can be added for you.

As the ancients said: "Investigation must be real investigation; awakening must be real awakening. Consider Layman Yanrong before he met the Fourth Patriarch, or Mazu before he met Nanyue—how could they have been like this [superficial] at that time?
Today’s students are guessing east and west; every one of them is dead-hearted and prostrate on their mats. Students!
One only knows the point where the mouth opens; one assumes it will be easy to find a place to settle and plant one's feet.
One does not know that before the mouth has opened, even Buddhas and Patriarchs find it difficult to draw near. A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the teaching of a lifetime? Yunmen said:
To speak of one as one. Now tell me, how much difference is there between this and when the World-Honored One ascended the seat and Mañjuśrī struck the gavel?
A monk asked Zhaozhou, “The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return? Zhaozhou said, “I am making a cotton shirt in Qingzhou that weighs seven catties.
Such words—whether from the past or present, far or near—are exactly the same. When the ancients reached this point...
It is said that each and every one of these resides within the great inconceivable ocean.

Formerly, when Master Xiangyan was at Mount Gui, he would answer ten for every one asked, and a hundred for every ten. Mount Gui, seeking to strike him where there is true practice and genuine realization, gave him a sharp blow.

Xiangyan did not know why this was so; he subsequently went to Nanyang to pitch his hut, and upon striking a bamboo stalk, he attained awakening. Later, when he appeared in the world, he said: "The old..."

The monk [Zhaozhou] spent forty years before finally achieving unity. Master Zhaozhou spent over twenty years doing nothing but eating porridge, using the toilet, and excreting urine—these being the only times his mind was distracted.
Gaofeng did not leave his "dead gate" for thirty years. My late teacher spent forty years with nothing but a single thought.
Master Changqing Lingxun sat until seven蒲團 (būtuan) were worn through. This mountain monk has been practicing *gongfu* for ten...
For three years, my body has not leaned or fallen over. Now, at over seventy years of age, I still contemplate birth and death; I have not yet dared to depart from right mindfulness (*samyak-smṛti*).

The ancients had every thought-moment (*citta-kṣaṇa*) within meditative concentration (*samādhi*), remaining undisturbed amidst birth and death. People today have every thought-moment in distraction, remaining unsettled amidst birth and death.
Do students still know what right mindfulness is? As previously stated, it is the profound realm of the Tathāgata.
It is so. When I, this mountain monk, was formerly at my late teacher’s place, he questioned me until I reached a point where there was no corner to grasp and no place to apply my hand;
I could not help but exert all my strength to overturn it, and my late teacher spoke the word "So. Looking back now, how much error there was in that!
Let things follow their conditions and accord with one's lot, and wait for the root of life to be severed. I have always applied my mind to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*; according to what I see:
When Sudhana visited the fifty-three spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), he never moved a single step; when those fifty-three spiritual friends instructed Sudhana, they never opened their mouths.

In my Sahā world-system, the Flower Treasury Ocean of Vairocana Tathāgata, every single character and every single phrase—indeed, all characters and all phrases—is fully endowed with as many [expressions] as there are atoms in the four continents.
It is taught that each successive turning is unspeakable. Each samādhi, each utterance, each ocean of fragrant water,
each Cakravāḍa mountain range, each Vairocana Flower Treasury world-realm, each Maitreya pavilion, each Buddha and Bodhisattva, each great spiritual friend,
and each observation of those Flower Treasuries of the Buddhas as they are taught— each is unspeakable.
The samādhi of eloquence; each and every samādhi of analytical eloquence; each and every unimpeded supernormal power;
each and every Buddha-world adorned by the spiritual power of the Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field;
and each and every gate of samādhi expounded by the World-Honored Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field—inconceivable, most subtle, and at the limit of the most subtle.

Thus one knows that the oceans of Buddha-treasuries and each of their samādhis— numbering as many as the atoms within a buddha-field— as taught by all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the fifty-three spiritual friends,
are [all contained] within my own self-enjoyment samādhi of the single reality (eka-tattva), which is the Tathāgata Vairocana.
Without increase or decrease, without "that" or "this," the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Flower Ornament Treasury Ocean, along with all spiritual friends,

each exhaustively employing their supernatural powers and samādhis, directed toward me a great ocean of inconceivable samādhis as numerous as the atoms within the Buddha-lands of the Vairocana Buddhas;
they turned unspeakable samādhis, each with its unique adornment and each with its unique syllable.
From each and every radiance of the mani-jewels, there arose jeweled couches and thrones as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field;
jeweled canopies and jeweled nets; jeweled trees and jeweled clouds; jeweled lotuses and jeweled necklaces—as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field.

There also arose clouds of lion banners, clouds of mani-jewel banners, clouds of lamps, clouds of flames, clouds of flower-flames, and clouds of incense-flames—as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field. Each and every... [buddha-field]...
Masses of light from mani-jewels as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field; the transformation bodies of Buddhas, adorned and manifested, as numerous as the atoms of each buddha-field;
spiritual friends of kingdoms and cities as numerous as the atoms of each buddha-field;

and furthermore, the mountains, rivers, great earth, and the myriad phenomena arrayed before one’s eyes, along with their various distinct sounds, various illusory manifestations, and various characteristics.

Excellent. This extends even to all the great hells, the eight cold and eight hot hells, the cycles of ten thousand deaths and ten thousand births, as well as the celestial pleasures of the Trāyastriṃśa heavens—each numbering as many as the atoms within a Buddha-field, unspeakable, unspeakable, and unspeakably beyond description.
Revolving and revolving, it is ineffable; it is entirely this Flower Garland Treasury-Ocean, the Samādhi of One True Reality.

Thus, the Flower Garland Treasury-Oceans as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, spiritual friends, devas, humans, and non-humans—all these are each individually as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, ineffable and ineffable, revolving and revolving.
It can be described. Yet, as they turn and transform, they are ineffable.

Each and every being of the four modes of birth and the six realms—whether wriggling insects, sentient creatures, or insentient things—is entirely contained within the number of atoms and sub-atomic particles of my Buddha-field, within this Flower Adornment Ocean-Treasury.
Each and every thing is interpenetrating and unimpeded. Thus do I, this mountain monk, speak;
thus do you all hear; thus do all Buddhas abide; thus do all sentient beings see. Sentient beings see thus;
all Buddhas abide thus; you all hear thus; I, this mountain monk, speak thus. Furthermore, each and every one hears, sees, abides, and speaks thus—one by one.
Regarding the motes of dust, grains of sand, blades of grass, and leaves: there are Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within those Buddha-fields.

Within each mote of dust, each grain of sand, each blade of grass, and each leaf, there are Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field. One passes through each of these Buddha-fields by means of a samādhi;
within each samādhi of each Buddha, there are worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, all of which are clearly perceived.
They are unobtainable. Yet I clearly perceive the various distinctions of each and every Buddha-world;
all are illusory transformations, and each is entirely unobtainable and beyond comprehension. I know that they are incomprehensible, invisible, and unobtainable.
I constantly abide in the samādhi of quiescence within a single thought-moment, seeking the dharma of quiescence; yet in reality, there is nothing [to be found].

All such things are thus within the state of quiescent mindfulness. Within this, all Buddhas, the oceans of samādhis as numerous as the atoms of all Buddha-fields, their various adornments, various worlds, various distinctions, various offerings, and the illusory manifestations of all Buddhas—I likewise have no thought regarding them.
By means of this non-thought toward the illusory manifestations of all Buddhas, every moment is fully endowed with mindfulness. Mindfulness.
To be mindful without deviation is called the Great Meaning of the Avataṃsaka Dharmadhātu. Regarding the teaching of illusory existence, such is the samādhi of illusory existence;
how much more so for the text of eighty-one fascicles and the discourse on the ten Dharma-realms?
It is inconceivable and beyond deliberation. To transcribe it all into a single fascicle—rolling it up and then unfolding it again—is, in this way, the eight... [fascicles].
The eleven scrolls and the misty waters of a hundred cities are all external matters; the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) are merely adventitious dust.

This does not hinder whether one acts in opposition to or in accordance with the flow, nor whether one speaks horizontally or vertically, or speaks in every atom and every world-system. Therefore, the Sūtras state:
"By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to courageously and diligently cultivate the path to omniscience. By associating with...
Virtuous friends can swiftly give birth to the ocean of all great vows.
By relying upon virtuous friends, one can expound the Dharma within a single atom so that it pervades the entire Dharma-realm. By relying upon virtuous friends, one acts in every thought-moment.
They ultimately abide in the stage of omniscience. By drawing near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), they are able to travel to the lands of the ten directions;

seeing spiritual friends with undistracted minds, seeing spiritual friends shatter the mountains of obstructions, seeing spiritual friends enter the ocean of great compassion to rescue and protect sentient beings, and seeing spiritual friends attain the light of wisdom that universally illumines the *dharmadhātu*.
By seeing a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one is able to behold universally the oceans of Buddhas of the ten directions.

By seeing a spiritual friend, one attains the vision of all Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma. Thus, one should properly seek out and study each successive stage of spiritual friends as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field;
likewise, one may inquire from the very beginning about the samādhis of all Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field. As for the spiritual friend—
There are such inconceivable, ineffable, and immeasurably boundless pure samādhis.
Those who wish to draw near to a spiritual friend must necessarily possess great causes and conditions and be endowed with unsurpassed wisdom;

having resolved upon the unsurpassed mind, they must remain without regression for hundreds of thousands of kalpas before finally attaining such correspondence. As for the Head Seat, he is like the Great Being Mañjuśrī.
Extending one arm across Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field, he touched the crown of Sudhana’s head;

yet this mountain monk, without moving from his seat, extended across Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field and, through the inconceivable samādhi of Śākyamuni Tathāgata within the Flower Treasury Ocean, spoke it forth in full flow from a single hair-tip. Now tell me, how does this compare with Mañjuśrī?
Are they the same? Are they different? Neither the same nor different. Both the same and both different. The Master threw away his brush and said, "The paper is exhausted.
He rolled it up.
*The Great Meaning of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra* (End).
